network.router.guide_ca_help: If the router lacks an already trusted HTTPS certificate, open System → Certificates. Create a CA named, for example, justvoxel-ca with Common Name justvoxel-ca, RSA 2048, and validity of about 3650 days. Enable Trusted. Select only key-cert-sign and crl-sign for Key Usage, then sign it as a self-signed root CA.
network.router.guide_leaf_help: Create a server certificate named, for example, www-ssl. The Common Name and Subject Alt Name (SAN) must match the router address or DNS name used in JustVoxel. For an IP SAN in WebFig, select IP as the type and enter only the address, without IP: or ::. Choose RSA 2048, validity of about 825 days, and Key Usage digital-signature, key-encipherment and tls-server. Sign it with your CA.
network.router.guide_leaf_sign_fallback: If WebFig refuses to sign the HTTPS server certificate, for example by showing “Selection expected!”, the router administrator can run /certificate sign <SERVER_CERTIFICATE_NAME> ca=<CA_CERTIFICATE_NAME> in RouterOS Terminal. Replace both placeholders with your certificate names. www-ssl and justvoxel-ca are example certificate names.
network.router.guide_upload_help: If you created a private CA, export only its public certificate as PEM, leaving the export passphrase blank. Download the .crt file from RouterOS and upload it in JustVoxel under Router → Connection. Enter the HTTPS endpoint, username and password. Test the connection, review the forwarding settings, then save.
network.router.guide_renew_help: When you renew the HTTPS server certificate with the same CA, JustVoxel can keep the uploaded CA. Use Replace CA when the signing CA changes.

network.router.guide_intro: Your router administrator can prepare MikroTik RouterOS here for JustVoxel’s read-only connection.
network.router.https_help: Assign the signed server certificate to www-ssl and enable the HTTPS service. Set rest-secure=yes and rest-plain=no. Keep WebFig, index and graphs enabled if you use them, or disable them for REST-only HTTPS access. The router administrator manages service address restrictions and input firewall rules.
network.router.group_help: Create a dedicated RouterOS group, for example jv, and grant it only the read, write, api and rest-api policies. REST authorization requires the api policy. The native RouterOS API service on TCP 8728 can stay disabled unless you use it for another purpose.
network.router.user_help: Create a dedicated RouterOS user, for example justvoxel, and assign it to your dedicated group. Where appropriate, limit Allowed Address to <JUSTVOXEL_IP>/32 and choose a strong, unique password on the router.
network.router.input_help: Your router administrator must allow the JustVoxel host to reach the HTTPS REST endpoint, normally <JUSTVOXEL_IP> → <ROUTER_IP>:443/TCP. Your administrator owns this security decision. JustVoxel will never create or modify router input or firewall filter rules.
network.router.forward_help: The firewall must allow legitimate destination NAT traffic to the JustVoxel host. The settings below are an example only, not a universal command. Adapt the WAN selection, destination, chains and rule order to your firewall. Place the allowance before any rule that would otherwise block the traffic. Some configurations already allow legitimate dstnat traffic and need no additional rule. JustVoxel will never create, move, enable, disable or delete this filter rule.
network.router.boundary_help: JustVoxel reads router identity and version and inspects NAT records for status and conflicts. A future release may manage only its own destination NAT (dstnat) records.
network.router.exclusions: Firewall filter and input rules, interfaces, VLANs, routes, DNS, DHCP, RouterOS users and groups, certificates, /ip service settings, packages and updates, router reboots and arbitrary RouterOS commands are outside the connector’s scope.
network.router.endpoints_help: Forwarding status uses ports from the existing Minecraft instance or Minecraft Network (Velocity) configuration. JustVoxel has no way to accept arbitrary ports.
